summary: Streaming chat sessions go silent mid-generation when prefetch throttle and corporate SSL proxy coincide
description: Issue summary: Several customers using Dedicated capacity reported streaming chat responses (SSE) that silently stall mid-generation. Impact: end-users see chats freeze with no final token and client-side eventually shows timeout/reconnect. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east, traffic routed through customer corporate SSL proxy; client uses SSE over HTTPS. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a long chat generation (>800 tokens) to redwood/gpt-medium-qa-v1 pinned on dedicated pool. 2) Repeat under corporate network that performs TLS interception and connection reuse. 3) Trigger high prefetch and KV-cache warmup by sending concurrent warmup requests (~20 concurrent). Observations/Logs: - Server shows continuous generation in runtime traces but no bytes reach client after ~40-120s. - Proxy logs show intermittent TLS session renegotiation and connection splice events. - Serving runtime reports prefetch-throttle events and worker backpressure in same timeframe. - Client SSE shows no close event; connection remains open but silent until client-side timeout. - No 5xx from edge; connections show long idle periods.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Patel: Customer DataSight reported multiple user sessions stalling mid-generation. They supplied client-side logs and our server traces. Opening ticket and assigned to infra SRE.
2026-03-10 11:05 - DataSight (via CS rep): "Their chat app shows spinner indefinitely; reconnects do not resume last generation. Works fine from home networks, fails behind corp VPN/proxy."
2026-03-11 14:20 - Ethan Zhao: Initial triage points to correlation between prefetch-throttle warnings and proxy TLS session events. Asked customer for proxy config and packet captures.
2026-03-12 08:45 - DataSight: Provided proxy vendor logs showing TLS session reuse and occasional renegotiation every ~60s. Policy enforces deep inspection on long-lived streams.

2026-03-13 16:30 - Priya Singh (Serving Runtime): Reproduced in staging by simulating TLS interceptor that resets stream parameters mid-KV-prefetch. Observed worker enters backpressure, runtime continues generating but chunk write to socket returns EPIPE intermittently.

2026-03-14 09:00 - Ethan Zhao: Rolling a targeted mitigation to Dedicated edge: increase SSE write heartbeats and add explicit chunk flush on token emission for affected pool; asking for monitoring window post-deploy.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 2026-03-09 first customer reports; 03-10 reproduce attempt in house. Metrics: surge of prefetch_throttle.count and serving_runtime.write_retries correlate with streaming silence windows. Hypotheses: 1) Corporate SSL proxy performs mid-stream TLS re-negotiation or connection splice that leaves long-lived HTTP/1.1 SSE connections in a half-open state leading to kernel-level write stalls. 2) Prefetch throttling causes the runtime to batch tokens longer, so there are fewer writes; combined with proxy coalescing this increases chance of proxy-triggered connection state change during quiet periods. Evidence: packet captures show server-side FIN+ACK after proxy splice while runtime still had queued bytes. Reproducible in staging with simulated TLS-interceptor that triggers renegotiation after idle intervals. Affected subset: Dedicated pools with aggressive KV-prefetch enabled and customers behind TLS inspection proxies. Observed that websocket clients show similar but less frequent symptoms due to different keepalive patterns. Logs and dashboards: link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-silence?var=pool=dedicated-us-east
resolution: Workaround: 1) Advise customers to allow passthrough of long-lived SSE/WebSocket streams at proxy level or configure proxy to avoid mid-stream renegotiation. 2) Temporary server-side mitigation deployed: enable frequent SSE heartbeat (every 8s) and force token-chunk flush on emission for the affected dedicated pool to reduce quiet windows. Fix: Implemented more robust socket-handling in serving-runtime to detect silent write backpressure and proactively close and retry stream with a short reconnect advisory (launch PR linked below). Rollout notes: mitigation rolled to 2 dedicated nodes in us-east on 2026-03-14 09:15 UTC, monitoring for 48h. Follow-ups: - Create advisory for customers behind TLS interceptors describing recommended proxy config. - Add a runtime metric to track proxy-splice events and increase test coverage by simulating TLS-intercept in CI.
